title: Tokaji Aszú
subtitle: The king of wines
objectives: Explain how Tokaji Aszú is made

steps.title: Aszú berries
steps.body: Aszú berries are individually picked, botrytised and shrivelled, almost raisins. They're stored as a paste, then soaked in fermenting must or a base wine for 12 to 60 hours, which extracts sugar and flavour. The mix is pressed and fermented slowly, then aged in small Gönci barrels in cold, damp cellars.
steps.highlight: Botrytised berries soaked in base wine

steps.title: Puttonyos
steps.body: Sweetness was measured in puttonyos: the number of 25 kg baskets, called puttony, of aszú berries added to a 136-litre Gönci barrel of base wine. From 3 to 6 puttonyos. Since 2013, Tokaji Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar, equal to the old 5 puttonyos, and the term puttonyos is optional.

options: Baskets of aszú berries per barrel
steps.explanation: The number of 25 kg baskets added to a 136-litre barrel.

steps.title: Eszencia
steps.body: Eszencia is the free-run juice that drips from aszú berries under their own weight. It can contain over 450 g/l of sugar, ferments for years and rarely exceeds 5% alcohol. It's one of the rarest, sweetest wines in the world, traditionally served by the spoon.
steps.highlight: Over 450 g/l, served by the spoon

steps.prompt: Put the making of Tokaji Aszú in order.
items: Soak in base wine or must
steps.explanation: Selection, soaking and slow fermentation give Aszú its depth.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aszú berries are soaked in base wine, then fermented slowly
Since 2013, Aszú needs at least 120 g/l of sugar
Eszencia is free-run juice with over 450 g/l
